title: Is there a square hiding among these tilted figures?
description: Four tilted figures on a dot grid are tested against the rule for a square: four equal sides and four corners like the corner of a book. The video counts dots across and down for each figure and finds the one square.
teaching_notes: One idea: a square needs equal sides and corners like a book corner, and equal sides alone are not enough. Watch for children who call figure B a square because its sides look equal.

source: Identify if there are any squares in this collection. Use measurements if needed.
video_script.why: The child uses the two properties of a square from the example in the book to test four tilted figures on a dot grid.
video_script.substitution: Four tilted figures on a dot grid, tested by counting dots across and down.
video_script.anchor: Four tilted figures A, B, C and D with their corners on the dots of a grid
video_script.payoff_line: Exactly one figure in the collection is a square.

final_answer.spoken: exactly one figure in the collection is a square, and it is figure eigh

never_show: the verdict on the figures before the answer
maths_rules: A: diamond 8 dots wide and 8 dots tall, so half-spans 4 and 4; every side goes 4 across and 4 down, so the 4 sides are equal, and the corners fit a book corner: a square.

B: diamond 6 dots wide and 8 dots tall, half-spans 3 and 4; every side goes 3 across and 4 down (3 x 3 + 4 x 4 = 9 + 16 = 25 = 5 x 5, so each side is 5 dot steps); sides equal but the top corner is sharper than a book corner: not a square.
C: diamond 10 dots wide and 8 dots tall, half-spans 5 and 4; sides equal but the top corner is wider than a book corner: not a square.
D: a small tilted rectangle with two long sides and two short sides: not a square.
Only A has four equal sides and four book corners.
video_script.design: One idea: a square needs equal sides and four book corners. Uses the two properties of the book example. The four figures stay all video.
open_questions: The sizes of the figures come from the item description, because the book text does not show the dot grid.
